tool_input.command:
python3 - <<'E'
p='src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts'
L=open(p).read().split('\n')
# lines 118-130 (1-based) Update block -> Partial
i=L.index('        Update: {',117-1) if False else 117
assert L[i]=='        Update: {' and L[i+12]=='        };'
L[i:i+13]=['        Update: Partial<ClientInsert>;']
# Insert block lines 105-117 -> alias
j=104
assert L[j]=='        Insert: {' and L[j+12]=='        };'
body=L[j+1:j+12]
L[j:j+13]=['        Insert: ClientInsert;']
alias=['type ClientInsert = {']+[l[4:] for l in body]+['};','']
k=L.index('export type Database = {')
L[k:k]=alias
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(L))
E
sed -n 10,30p src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts; node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run 2>&1 | tail -15

resultText:
I fixed the one finding from attempt 1, the duplication in `src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts`. The full vitest run passes: 27 files, 187 tests.

The `clients` table's `Insert` and `Update` types repeated the same 9 lines. I pulled the fields into one `ClientInsert` type. `Insert` now uses it, and `Update` is `Partial<ClientInsert>`. The resulting types are the same as before.

Everything else from attempt 1 was already staged: the migration, `insurance.ts`, the card, the page and the action, and `docs/conformance.md`. I didn't change any of it this round.

What I couldn't check:
- I didn't run `node scripts/factory-tap.mjs`.
- I didn't check whether the other tables in `database.types.ts` (for example `holds`) have the same Insert/Update repetition. The maintainability finding only named the `clients` block.
- I didn't run the migration against a real database. The visible tests passing is the only evidence it works.
- The production UAT for AC-INS-06 is outside this task.
